title: Loopback ring takes a one-pair dup while priming after a bind at INTERNAL (simulation)
body:
**Observation (simulation, pre-existing on `dev`).** In the `follow_ring` harness, a listener bind at INTERNAL whose primed margin lies inside B17's window can move `SLIP_LB` by +1 dup. That is one loopback pair, half the +2 frame unit B17 measured. It happens 0.13 to 0.25 ms after the bind's first PDU, before any settle recentre acts.

**Evidence:** [R634-1 on PR #742](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/742#issuecomment-6193454471), finding F2, with receipts in its review archive.
- **32 phases, 0 to 5 us lateness:** 1 of 141 in-window binds (`bind_j5_p27`, phase 0.84375, seed 672, B17 cycle 7).
- **Dense cycle-7 scan, 128 phases:** 2 of 132 in-window binds (phases 0.8906 and 0.9297).
- **Determinism:** the result repeats on a rerun, and `dev`'s datapath shows the same +1 at the same instant. The bind-arm change in PR #742 neither causes nor removes it.
- **Bench:** B17 never showed a one-pair dup. It showed only +2 frame slips at the first burst.

**Reproduce** (pinned Verilator 5.050), on PR #742's head and on `dev`:
`Vfollow_ring --case bind --bind-phase 0.843750 --jitter-us 5 --seed 672 --any-phase --dwell-s 0.5`

**To establish:**
1. The mechanism. The reviewer's lead is pair-asymmetric commit and pop timing around priming in the unchanged capture crossbar (`KL_chan_map_capture`).
2. Whether it is the DUT or a harness stimulus artefact.
3. Whether the two loopback pairs leave lockstep afterwards.

This matters because #645's post-merge bench repeat grades an unchanged `SLIP_LB` across each bind.

Relates to #645.
